question: Should OpenClaw add an opt-in execute-on-parse tool scheduling mode in core now, or wait until tool concurrency-safety metadata is defined first?
rationale: The source-level latency gap is clear, but the fix changes core runtime semantics and safety policy rather than repairing a narrowly broken existing contract.

options.title: Design Opt-In Core Mode
options.body: Keep this issue open and require an owner design covering safety metadata, transcript ordering, hooks, approvals, cancellation, and regression proof before implementation.

options.title: Block On Tool Safety Metadata
options.body: Treat this as blocked until https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/62962 or an equivalent concurrency-safety contract exists.

options.title: Defer Semantics Change
options.body: Keep the current post-stream batching model if maintainers decide early execution is too risky for now.

recommendation.title: Design Opt-In Core Mode
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and require an owner design covering safety metadata, transcript ordering, hooks, approvals, cancellation, and regression proof before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged work and follow-up commits show direct involvement in the adjacent tool-call stream boundary that would need the product decision.
